title: ScaleDown SLM_Agent and DietCode, from the owner's message
source: The owner's message of 2026-10-14 (repo link, `npm install -g dietcode`, `dietcode setup`, docs.scaledown.ai/quickstart). Dossier by `python -m faceless intake`; the quickstart page was read with WebFetch. Nothing was installed or run.

items.name: SLM Agent (scaledown-team/SLM_Agent, npm @scaledown/migration-agent)
items.why: It is not a Claude Code token saver. Its README says it scans an application's code for AI API calls and migrates them to ScaleDown's paid small-model API (compress, classify, extract, summarize), which needs SCALEDOWN_API_KEY and sends our prompts to a third party. No licence file was found, it has 33 weekly downloads, and its install runs unpinned code. The `dietcode` package the owner named is a different thing: neither the repo's README nor the quickstart page describes it or what `dietcode setup` changes, so it cannot be reviewed. A tool that installs hooks into Claude Code's own settings and may route session context to an outside service needs its code read first.
items.steal: The idea of compressing long context before a model call. The engine's own calls are small (Haiku at about $0.003 a song); the real token burn is this long session, not the pipeline.
items.owner: If you still want DietCode: send its README or repo link so it can be read, say whether sending session context to ScaleDown is acceptable, and confirm a key is yours to use. Install it on your own computer, since it edits local Claude Code settings; it cannot work in this cloud container.
